snapshot.exam_hook: 🏔️ UPSC Environment Hook: Hotspots: 4 in India. In-situ: Home. Ex-situ: Away. CR: GIB. EN: Tiger. Alpha: Site. First NP: Jim Corbett (originally Hailey National Park, 1936).

quick_notes.title: Levels of Biodiversity
quick_notes.detail: Alpha (within site), Beta (between sites), Gamma (total/landscape). Genetic, Species, and Ecosystem diversity.

quick_notes.title: In-situ Conservation
quick_notes.detail: Protecting species in their natural habitat. 1. National Parks : High protection, no human activity. 2. Wildlife Sanctuaries : Limited activity allowed. 3. Biosphere Reserves : Core (no activity), Buffer, Transition.

quick_notes.title: Ex-situ Conservation
quick_notes.detail: Protecting species outside their natural habitat. 1. Botanical Gardens. 2. Zoos. 3. Gene Banks/Seed Banks. 4. Cryopreservation.

quick_notes.title: Biodiversity Hotspots
quick_notes.detail: Must have 1, 500 endemic vascular plants and lost 70% of original habitat. India has 4: Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, Sundaland.

quick_notes.title: IUCN Red List
quick_notes.detail: Categories: Extinct, Critically Endangered (Critically Endangered), Endangered (Endangered), Vulnerable (VU). India examples : Great Indian Bustard (Critically Endangered), Tiger (Endangered).

lesson_intro: Today we study the 'Library of Nature'. Biodiversity is the variety of life on Earth. We explore the 'Levels of Biodiversity' (Alpha, Beta, Gamma) and the 'In-situ' vs 'Ex-situ' methods of conservation. For UPSC, focus on 'Biodiversity Hotspots' in India, 'Red List categories' of IUCN, and the location of major National Parks. Let's master the protection of our natural heritage today.
